text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bomb explosion kills 11 people in the western city of Relizane on Algeria's voting day on Thursday. Security forces shot daed 10 "terrorists" in Blida, south of Algiers, on the same day. A civilian was also assassinated in Blida.

- An editorial by El Watan's editor Omar Belhouchet on the referendum results. "Did the government cheat on the vote's results in order to show the high figures announced by Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour?" wrote Belhouchet.
- Foreign reporters complain about difficulties they encountered during the referendum. They say the authorities denied them free movement because of the security situation.
- Official figures show huge "yes" for the draft constitution. Opposition parties contest the results as officially announced by the government.
- Security forces defused several bombs set to explode during Thursday's referendum.
- Bomb explosion killed at least two in a cafe shop in Baraki, near Algiers, on voting day.
- Voters triumph over fear. More than 85 percent of the electorate say "yes" to the constitution change.
